transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-05-22
Time: 11:00 AM PT (scheduled 11:00-11:52)
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (Cassiopeia Head of Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Security Architect), Priya Sharma (Finance), Devon Brooks (Platform Eng)

Summary: Short preflight between procurement, security and Redwood to align on licensing (committed vs on-demand), egress costing, DPA redlines and next steps to enable pilot. Some clarifying Qs on KMS, SSO and private deployment options.

Topics: pricing tiers / commit scenarios, egress fees, Dedicated vs Hosted fallback, DPA/MSA redline items, pilot scope and timelines, security deep dive (KMS/HSM, audit logs)

Notes/Links shared: Pricing spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example/pricing/CRM-78422), DPA-redlines-v1.docx (link: drive/attachments/DPA-CR-78422), benchmark-csv (link: s3://benchmarks/cassiopeia-dedicated.csv)

Transcript: 
[00:00] Avery: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Uh we're gonna run about 50 minutes here, quick preflight to align on procurement and security asks before you loop in legal. Marta, thanks for coordinating.
[00:12] Marta: Yeah thanks. We wanted to surface a couple of big questions — primarily around how committed licensing works, and how egress will be billed if we put some traffic through a Dedicated pool.
[00:25] Riley: Cool. I'll try to keep the infra details clear — so Redwood has a few product paths: our hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem options. Sorry if product names get fuzzy in the notes, I say Redwood Dedicate sometimes, forgive me.
[00:41] Liam: Quick clarification, when you say egress, do you mean network egress costs from your cloud or the tokenized billing egress — like model token units and compute? Because finance wants to separate network egress (cloud) vs per-token unit pricing.
[00:56] Priya: Yes that's right, we need both lines. Also curious how burst capacity is charged if we exceed committed throughput.
[01:06] Avery: Good call. On the commercial side we usually split it: per-token generation/embedding charge + optional committed throughput discount. Network egress (cloud provider data transfer) is separate and typically billed back at cost; for Dedicated you can choose to bring-your-own-cloud or let Redwood manage. If Redwood-managed, network egress passes through our billing with a small handling fee.
[01:28] Devon: For pilot we'll probably run mixed workloads — some chat, some long form generation, and higher KV cache reuse for chat. Does the Dedicated runtime support KV cache persistence across pods? We want predictable latencies.
[01:41] Riley: Yes — runtime supports continuous batching and KV-cache techniques, but small note: the cache persistence semantics vary by deployment. On Dedicated managed pools we offer sticky routing to keep KV hot; in private VPC installs you can configure a shared stateful cache. There was a note in our benchmark doc about sequences with heavy context causing more memory pressure and slightly higher token p99.
[02:06] Marta: On the DPA side our legal team redlined a couple clauses — data retention, sub processors, and audit log retention. We sent DPA-redlines-v1 earlier. Can you confirm Redwood's standard retention window and whether separate retention controls are available for Dedicated?
[02:21] Jordan: Right, standard hosted retention is 30 days for logs by default but can be extended as an add-on. For Dedicated, the customer can opt for zero retention or local only logs; we also support integrations with KMS and HSM for keying. Note — sometimes our public docs say KMS but customers want H S M level control, we can map that.
[02:42] Liam: Ok I'd like to see the KMS flow. Specifically: where keys are stored, access controls, rotation and whether Redwood ever sees plaintext.
[02:51] Riley: Short answer: for Redwood-managed keys we use KMS with envelope encryption. For private installs you can inject your own keys via Cloud KMS or HSM; in those cases Redwood does not have the unwrap keys. We'll capture the exact flow in the security deep dive.
[03:08] Priya: Back to pricing — can you walk through a sample committed tier? Like 200k tokens per minute or something? We need to model monthly spend to present to finance.
[03:19] Avery: Sure — rough example: On hosted with no commit it's per-token at X cents. With a commit (reserved throughput) you get a 25% discount on per-token rate up to the committed throughput and lower unit rates beyond. For Dedicated reserved pools pricing is more complex (monthly capacity reservation + per-token). I'll send a pricing spreadsheet with multiple scenarios — light commit, medium commit, and heavy commit — and include egress knobs.
[03:44] Marta: And burst? If we commit 2 GPUs worth of throughput but have a spike, how does Redwood handle bursts?
[03:51] Riley: We have a burst capacity setting — you can enable a burst buffer which will be billed at a premium per-token when used. There's also autoscaling for Dedicated pools but that requires lead time and often a capacity buffer in contract.
[04:07] Devon: For the pilot we want to test tail-latency and cost under production-like loads. Can Redwood run a scheduled benchmark that hits our routing policy and returns latency distribution and per-token cost?
[04:18] Avery: Yes. We can run a bench with your sample traces or synthetic traffic. We'll share the benchmark-csv and a short runbook for how to reproduce; Riley will own the test config.
[04:31] Liam: On the MSA — one point from our counsel: liability caps and data incident notifications. Does Redwood have a standard notification timeline and SLA credits?
[04:43] Jordan: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated pools; the MSA includes standard incident notification windows (we aim to notify within 24 hours of detection). SLA credits are tiered and tied to uptime percentages. Legal can negotiate specific windows during enterprise contract process.
[04:58] Marta: Our procurement also asked about export controls and data residency. Some of our customers in EMEA require data to stay within region. Is regional pinning supported?
[05:10] Riley: Absolutely. We have per-region hosting. For Dedicated we can pin capacity to a region; for private VPC we can deploy into your region. We'll note any egress differences per region in the pricing.
[05:22] Priya: One more finance nuance — if we sign a commit for say six months, what's the billing cadence and refund policy if usage is below commit?
[05:32] Avery: Typical reserved capacity contracts are monthly billed and non-refundable; unused committed units don't usually roll back but we can design smoothing rules in the contract (e.g., bank across quarters) — we'll surface these options in the pricing spreadsheet.
[05:46] Marta: We also want to know who signs the procurement order internally — need names for the approval chain. I'll send that after this call.
[05:55] Jordan: Great. On the security docs, I'll attach SOC 2 and current pen test summary in the follow-up; Liam, if you have specific control matrix items we'll map them.
[06:03] Liam: Yeah I'll forward the control matrix; initial ask is: does Redwood support SSO via SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and audit log streaming to our SIEM?
[06:15] Riley: Yes — SSO SAML and OIDC both; RBAC is supported with per-role entitlements and audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog or object storage. For private installs we also offer agent forwarding.
[06:29] Priya: Can you confirm encryption-at-rest defaults? Our counsel asks about default encryption and options for customer-managed keys.
[06:36] Jordan: Default encryption at rest is on in all deployments. For hosted we manage the keys but can enable CMK (customer-managed keys) via cloud KMS; for private we support HSM-backed key stores. We'll outline the exact statements in the security deep dive doc.
[06:51] Marta: On DPA redlines we had two specific asks: narrower subprocessor clause and stricter deletion obligations. Any early pushback?
[07:00] Avery: We typically accept reasonable subprocessor transparency and provide a list and 30-day notice for changes. Deletion obligations — we can do contract language for stricter deletion for Dedicated and private deployments, but hosted may have a standard retention path; again this is negotiable in enterprise DPA.
[07:16] Devon: For the pilot, who will set up the onboarding? Can we get a runbook and a gate checklist? We want to avoid surprises.
[07:24] Jordan: Yes — Jordan will create a pilot runbook and onboarding checklist with connectivity steps (VPC peering or private link options), KMS handshake, and test harness.
[07:33] Riley: I'll include the benchmarking parameters and a short script to hit the token p50/p90/p99 capacities and KV-cache warmup steps.
[07:41] Marta: Sounds good. Can we tentatively schedule the legal review call? Counsel availability is next week on Wednesday afternoon.
[07:49] Avery: We'll propose Wed 2026-05-27 at 2pm ET for the legal-only review; I'll put a placeholder and send calendar invites after this.
[07:57] Priya: For the committed pricing, can you show a scenario where we cap monthly spend at a not-to-exceed and Redwood guarantees that rate? Finance needs a predictable number.
[08:09] Avery: We can put a not-to-exceed structure in the quote — it's common to do a committed monthly cap with overage terms. I'll model a conservative usage curve in the spreadsheet.
[08:20] Liam: A technical Q — if we run private deployment with our own keys, how is the telemetry handled? We don't want payload telemetry leaving our VPC.
[08:31] Riley: In private mode telemetry can be restricted to local only, and logs streamed to your SIEM; we can disable central telemetry collection on request. We'll document the exact toggles you can set.
[08:44] Jordan: I'll attach SOC2, pen test summary and an architecture sketch that shows dedicated pool vs private VPC options.
[08:53] Marta: Great. Last thing — can you include a contact for escalation and post-sale onboarding team? We need names for our vendor panel.
[09:01] Avery: Yes — I'll include Jordan (CSM), Riley (SE) for technical, and the enterprise onboarding lead on the follow-up.
[09:09] Marta: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[09:12] Avery: Thanks — recap: Avery sends pricing spreadsheet and not-to-exceed scenarios; Jordan sends SOC2/pen test and pilot runbook; Riley schedules bench and security deep dive; Cassiopeia provides stakeholder list and DPA comments. We'll aim to reconvene after legal reviews.
[09:33] (audio: brief side conversation / mute noise)
[09:40] END

Recorded notes: transcript has occasional transcription errors ("Dedicate" for Dedicated, "K V cache" for KV cache etc.), speaker labels approximate.
